headline: TikTok owner ByteDance is reportedly close to a deal to buy custom AI chips for its data centres from Taiwan's MediaTek.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a reported deal in talks, single-source, but large spending involved.
importance_line: It could shift business between chip suppliers such as MediaTek, Broadcom, Qualcomm and Nvidia as ByteDance builds out its AI, but it is a report of talks, not a signed contract.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Stocktwits, that ByteDance, the owner of TikTok, is in talks to buy custom AI chips (application-specific integrated circuits, built for particular tasks) from Taiwan's MediaTek for its data centres. Bloomberg also reported that ByteDance is considering capital spending of up to $70 billion this year, more than double last year, and that MediaTek expects about $2 billion of AI-chip sales this year.
notes: Bloomberg page behind a bot wall; text read via Stocktwits on TradingView, which credits Bloomberg.
